changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6681-declared-lazy-marketplace-routes.md`

- names `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Both marketplace chunks were held by CHUNK CO-TENANCY, not by any import of the page: rolldown had parked `components/SuggestedBindingsPanel.tsx` (statically imported by the eager `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`) in the first, and `console/marketplace/InstalledListWidget.tsx` (bare-imported by the package barrel for its SDUI registration) in the second. An `app-shell-eager-leaves` group in `apps/console/vite.config.ts` isolates those co-tenants so the three declared-lazy pages chunk by their own dynamic-only reachability. The console eager closure moves 3180.2 KB → 3171.5 KB gzipped (−8,888 bytes, 48 → 45 eager chunks) with the three per-chunk ceilings unmoved.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `39e625de2` (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1801 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2409 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36704016808)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e4e32f71a4e6ef2f569fdaeaf021ba9206ab0d6c`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #11189 (body; triage `5907700357`, claim `5908486829`, dev report `5909622999`), PR #11202 (body, 3-file list, net diff against `main` `39e625de2`, which is `main`'s tip at review time), the check-runs on the head with `filter=latest`, and the head and `main` copies of `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` read for context. Nothing built, run, or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Each judgment is the diff read against the card's direction (triage `5907700357`) and the claim's region.

1. **Both defects reproduced on base `81778b955` (5 red / 1 green).** The dev's claim, not re-run. Judged consistent with the code as it stood: on `main` the toggle closed editing at once (its `setEditNav` flipped the flag in the click handler) and the autosave's `!editNav` block cleared the pending timer, so pins 1, 3 and 5 are red by construction; `doNavSave`'s unconditional `setNavDirty(false)` and the unconditional `setAppDraft(body)` in the load make pins 4 and 6 red; the clean-Done control is green on both. Right.

2. **The Done flush.** "Done" now sets `navClosing`; the effect beside the nav autosave runs `if (!navClosing || navSaving) return; if (navDirty && flushNavSave()) return; setNavClosing(false); if (navDirty) return; setEditNav(false); setNavSel(null);`. Read: a dirty buffer is sent at once (the flush, under the autosave's own `blocked`), a save in flight is waited out (`navSaving`), an edit taken during that save is flushed as soon as it lands (pin 5, inside 1 s), and the close happens only over a clean buffer. A failed send leaves `navDirty` true with the snapshot already attempted, so `flush` returns false, `navClosing` is cleared and editing stays open with the error on screen (pin 3). The "Edit" branch is unchanged (`setEditNav(true); setNavSel(null)`). `flush` is a `useState` initializer, so its identity is stable and it is a legal effect dependency. The hook's effects are declared before the closing effect, so `pendingRef` is current when `flush` reads it. Right.

3. **`navGen` and the generation-guarded clear.** `onNavPatch` is the only `setNavDirty(true)` site in the file, and both nav edit sources (the `AppNavCanvas` `onPatch` and the nav-item inspector's `onNavPatch`) go through it; it bumps `navGen` in the same update as the buffer patch. `doNavSave` captures `sentGen = navGen` in the render whose `appDraft` it sends (both are in its deps), and after the await clears `navDirty` only when `navCommittedRef.current.gen === sentGen`. The read-only put-back and the load's install do not bump the generation, as they are not edits. **Is `navGen` a second dirty flag?** No: it is a monotonic counter that is never reset and never read as a boolean; `navDirty` remains the only flag the leave guard, the copilot hold, the autosave and the closing effect read. `navCommittedRef` is a ref mirror of the same two states written by one effect for the two readers that land after an await; it is not an independently maintained flag. Judged a generation counter, as the direction allows. Right.

4. **The load effect's install guard.** `if (!isSameApp || !navCommittedRef.current.dirty) setAppDraft(body);` skips the install on a same-package re-read over a dirty buffer and still installs on a package switch (`isSameApp` is the pre-existing objectui#7255 identity check). `navBaselineRef`, `navHasDraft`, `appStatus` and the first-leaf selection still update on the skipped path, so a later read-only put-back uses the newer body. The deferred install lands on the re-read the sending save signals. Right.

5. **The widening into the shared `useDraftAutoSave` hook** (same file, outside the claimed lines; the dev's deviation 1). The hook is module-private (no export), so no public surface moves. The changes: the return type `void` becomes a stable function returning a boolean; a `pendingRef` written in the existing no-deps effect; a `flush` that fires the same send under the same `dirty`, `blocked` and already-attempted conditions and marks the snapshot attempted; a timer-callback guard `if (lastAttemptRef.current === snapKey) return;`. For the page inspector (`:2109`), the Data pillar (`:3314`) and the Automations pillar (`:4225`) the return is discarded, `flush` is never called, and the only other writer of `lastAttemptRef` is the timer itself, which the effect-level check already gated, so the new guard is never the deciding branch there. Behaviour-unchanged for the three. Right, and the minimal mechanism for the flush.

6. **The merge of `main` `39e625de2` (objectui#11181) and the load-effect conflict.** The head keeps `main`'s two `bodyLabel` lines verbatim (`const bodyLabel = (body.label ?? body.name) as I18nLabel | undefined; if (bodyLabel != null) setAppLabel(bodyLabel);`) with the guarded install directly below them. The net diff against `main` has 8 hunks, none in the app-label region (`resolvePackageApp`, the effect's `setAppLabel` lines, `ObjectActionsPanel`), and `ObjectActionsPanel.tsx` is not in the file list. Right.

7. **PR objectui#11187's effect and suite.** The objectui#11167 effect (its comment and body, 30 lines) is byte-identical between `main` and the head. `StudioDesignSurface.navEditClosesOnReadOnly-11167.test.tsx` exists at the head and is not in the PR's file list. Its green is CI's: see the check-runs line below. Right.

8. **The 3 ablation legs.** The dev's claim, not re-run. Each leg's red set is the one the mechanism predicts: without the flush, pins 1, 3 and 5 (a save expected at once, or inside 1 s, arrives a debounce later or never); without the generation guard, pins 4 and 5 (the clear drops the later edit); without the install guard, pins 4 and 6 (the re-read installs over the buffer), while pin 5 stays green because its flush sends before that re-read's requests return. Consistent. Right.

9. **Pins.** Done inside the debounce saves (pin 1); an Add during an in-flight save stays on screen and lands in the next save (pin 4); the leave guard holds until the last edit is sent (pins 4 and 5); the read-only close is unchanged (item 7). All four of the direction's pins are pinned in `StudioDesignSurface.navAutosaveFlush-11189.test.tsx`.

10. **One edge, named and escalated, not a defect of this card's shape.** The closing effect's comment reads `flush() === false` as "the save it already attempted failed, and its error is on screen". `flush` also returns false when the buffer has been edited back to exactly the last successfully sent snapshot within a debounce (the hook keys "attempted" by snapshot content, and `navDirty` is set by every edit): `navDirty` is then stale-true, nothing is unsent, and "Done" is inert with no cue. The stale-dirty itself is pre-existing since objectui#5813 on all four callers (on `main` the same sequence leaves the leave guard held for good). Nothing is lost, no pin or direction line is breached, and the fix belongs where the sent snapshot lives: it rides the proposed `useDraftAutoSave` family card (③ item 5), where clearing dirty for the sent snapshot resolves it for the four callers at once.

**Check-runs on `e4e32f71a`** (`filter=latest`): 11 runs were still in progress when this review began (10:48Z); the review waited in the foreground until every run had completed (the last, the `Test` rollup that appeared once the shards settled, at 10:55:49Z; inside the 25-minute cap). Final tally, 43 runs: 40 `success`, 3 `skipped` (the two coverage matrix placeholders and `dependabot`, none a gate for this diff), 0 failed, 0 in progress. The 8 test shards, `Lint`, `Type Check`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Build and E2E`, `Test (dist pins)`, the five changeset runs, the `Inert vi.mock Specifier Check` and the `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are all green. These conclusions are the gate verdicts; the objectui#11167 suite's green is inside the shards.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/11189-nav-autosave-flush-generation.md`: `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`. The diff changes internal editor state in one package: `InterfacesPillar`'s props are unchanged, `useDraftAutoSave` is module-private, no type, schema, prop or accepted set moves, and no other package is touched. `patch` is the level the diff publishes. The five changeset check-runs (Declaration, Bump Policy, Claim Re-read, Fixed Group, Overwrite Report) are green. `Clause-②: no`, as the PR body and the claim state, is right: nothing that Clause ② governs moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` is empty. Each deviation and out-of-scope note in the dev report (`5909622999`), answered:

1. **Deviation 1, the shared hook widened outside the claimed lines.** Answered in ① item 5: judged right. The flush had no other home, the hook is module-private, and the three other callers are behaviour-unchanged. The claim's "stop on breach" was met by naming it in the report and the PR body; no competing claim on the hook (objectui#11181's region was the app-label reads, landed and merged in). Accepted.

2. **Deviation 2, three ablation legs instead of two.** The install guard is a third mechanism with its own red set (① item 8). More coverage than the claim named. Accepted.

3. **Deviation 3, the one-minute lint-baseline copy in the tree.** Not in the head: the file list is the changeset, the pin suite and the source. The locked run's closure build (`--filter=@object-ui/app-shell^...`) excludes app-shell itself, and the type-check and directory test run started after the removal with bookends at dirty=0. CI on the head runs on a tree without it. Accepted.

4. **Out-of-scope (1), the PackageSwitcher's spurious draft after a confirmed discard.** Class a, measured, identical readings on `81778b955` and the branch, so pre-existing and not introduced here. The opposite shape to this card's (something unedited is sent, on a package the author only opened), so it does not ride the card. **Escalated to the seat to file as its own card**: the pillar is not keyed by package, the `!isSameApp` install replaces the buffer while `navDirty` and `editNav` stay set, and the autosave writes a draft row on the switched package. It is a write to a package the author did not edit, so grade it above a cosmetic p3.

5. **Out-of-scope (2), the in-flight-save loss on the hook's three other callers.** The Automations pillar was measured; the Data pillar and the page inspector were read only, and all three write the same post-await unconditional clear. This is the family's shape on the other editors. **Escalated to the seat**: one family closure card with the fix in `useDraftAutoSave` (the hook owns the sent snapshot and the post-save clear), as the dev proposes, is the right shape; it also takes the stale-dirty edge in ① item 10. The nav sites are closed here; the card's "a later nav-autosave site rides this card" does not reach non-nav sites.
